source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS016549, citing ID Tech Wire

redFlags.label: Third-party investigative platform
redFlags.detail: The Austin Police Department entered a contract for LexisNexis's Accurint Virtual Crime Center investigative platform in May 2023.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS013218, citing Austin

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Austin Police Department started its drone program in 2019. As of late 2021, the agency has 16 DJI Mavics and one Skydio drone.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS010082, citing Drone Life

redFlags.label: Real-time crime center
redFlags.detail: The Austin Police Department has operated a real-time crime center since 2010. The RTCC cost about $750,000 and was paid for without city funds through a federal grant. The RTCC accesses a network of 1000 H.A.L.O., or High Activity Location Observation, surveillance cameras throughout the city.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS006546, citing Strategic Partnerships Inc.

redFlags.label: Private camera registry
redFlags.detail: The Austin Police Department maintains a voluntary registry of private and personal surveillance cameras.
